title: Bounds on the Erdős-Rado number k(6,3): 30 ≤ k(6,3) ≤ 32 (Erdős Problem #112)
abstract: A Lean 4 proof that 30 ≤ k(6,3) ≤ 32. Here k(n,3) is the Erdős-Rado number: the least k such that every oriented graph on k vertices has n vertices with no arc between any two of them, or a transitive triangle (vertices x, y, z with arcs x → y, y → z and x → z). The lower bound is an explicit oriented graph on 29 vertices with no transitive triangle and no 6 independent vertices. The upper bound shows that every oriented graph on 32 vertices has one or the other; it rests on a counting argument and on one finite case analysis (every oriented graph on 14 vertices with no transitive triangle and no 4 independent vertices is 6-regular), which is carried out by 49 computations inside Lean's kernel. The upper bounds k(3,3) ≤ 9, k(4,3) ≤ 15 and k(5,3) ≤ 23 are proved on the way and are not cited. The whole proof is checked by the kernel, with no native_decide, and uses only the axioms propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice. Before this work the bounds that followed from published results were 26 ≤ k(6,3) ≤ 33. The result gives bounds only: k(6,3) is 30, 31 or 32, its value is not determined, and Erdős Problem #112, which asks for k(n,m) in general, remains open. As of 14 November 2026 the community database of Erdős problems lists #112 as unformalized, and the public Lean statements of the problem known to the author prove no bound; to the author's knowledge this is the first machine-checked result on the problem.
